question: Türkiye is seeking EU accession and yet it is making no headway in finding a solution to the Cyprus problem and is providing military support to the occupied territories of the Republic of Cyprus in the form of military equipment. Just a few weeks ago, Erdoğan made fresh inflammatory remarks, talking once again about a twostate solution for Cyprus, which is an EU Member State.

What is more, shipping activity has intensified, with ships transporting military equipment from Türkiye to the occupied territories. This raises questions about Ankara’s intentions. In view of this: 1.

What steps is the Commission taking to ensure that the transportation of new military equipment to the occupied territories of the Republic of Cyprus will not jeopardise the safety of an EU Member State?
Does it consider the transportation of this military equipment to be a cause for concern?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.6.2024) The EU’s full commitment to a comprehensive settlement to the Cyprus problem, within the United Nations (UN) framework, in accordance with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions and in line with the principles on which the Union is founded and the acquis, has been repeatedly emphasized by the European Council through its Conclusions.

Most recently, the European Council welcomed the appointment of María Angela Holguín Cuéllar as the UN Secretary-General’s Personal Envoy on Cyprus and stressed the readiness of the EU to play an active role in supporting all stages of the UN-led process1.

The High Representative/Vice-President (HR/VP) underlined in his statement of 18 August 20232 that, for this settlement to be possible in the future, also in line with the press statement of the UN Security Council of 12 July 20233, it remains essential to avoid unilateral actions, including actions that violate the military status quo along the ceasefire lines or result in an encroachment into the buffer zone.

The EU will also continue to emphasize that reducing tensions on both sides remains important for the process to move forward. The EU, including through the HR/VP, continues to communicate to Turkish officials the fact that a constructive engagement on the Cyprus issue remains essential also for the further enhancement of EU-Türkiye cooperation.
This was also emphasized in the European Council Conclusions of 17 April 20244.
